clue.text: Publication not available to carry a declaration of rights

parts.note: a magazine, shortened to mag, is a publication
to cart something is to carry it

explanation.surface: A periodical that cannot be had is asked to carry a statement of rights.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1215 charter sealed by King John set out rights and liberties, and is the archetypal declaration of them.

clue.text: Dressing always fixed by doctor

indicators.note: always is fixed in place by the doctor, held inside it

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
ay (also aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A wound dressing is always applied by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' suggests bandages; it is the salad sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo, short for mayonnaise, is a salad dressing.

clue.text: Wealth perhaps, good and ancient

parts.note: old means ancient

explanation.surface: Riches, perhaps, that are worthy and very old.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold is a form of riches, an example of wealth, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Ornate chapel prepared for parliamentary term

indicators.note: the letters of ornate chapel are made ready in a new order

explanation.surface: An elaborate chapel is made ready for a session of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term' looks like a session; it is a word or phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: In the UK Parliament each House traditionally refers to the other as 'another place' rather than by name.

clue.text: Discharged, having only some scarce duties

indicators.note: only part of the words scarce duties is used, the answer lying within them

explanation.surface: Someone dismissed from the army had few tasks left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharged' suggests dismissal; here it is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: Electricity arcs when it discharges across a gap as a spark, so arced is a past tense of discharging that way.

clue.text: Such a casual remark: 'Worth moving somewhere else?'

indicators.note: the letters of worth are moved about into a new order

parts.note: away means somewhere else

explanation.surface: A dismissive comment asks whether relocation would be worthwhile.
explanation.definitionFit: A throwaway remark is one made casually, as if in passing.

clue.text: Ruler's occult arts

definitions.note: read as 'Ruler is', the 's being a link to the wordplay

indicators.note: occult arts are mysterious and hidden, so the word arts is disguised by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A monarch dabbles in magic and the dark arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occult' looks like it describes the arts, but it signals that ARTS is rearranged; the 's on 'Ruler' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia, an absolute monarch and so a ruler.

clue.text: Girlfriend has case for musical instrument

parts.note: squeeze is informal for a girlfriend or partner
a box is a case

explanation.surface: A woman's partner owns a case for her instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeezebox is a colloquial name for an accordion or concertina.

clue.text: Admitted to hotel, deter moving on to rest of Bognor

indicators.note: the rearranged deter is put on to the end of the other piece

parts.note: Bognor Regis is an English seaside town, so Regis is the rest of its name

indicators.note: the letters of deter are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A guest checks into a hotel, which puts them off travelling on to the rest of Bognor.
explanation.walkthrough: Bognor Regis is a seaside resort on England's south coast, so 'rest of Bognor' is the second word of its name; 'moving' shuffles 'deter', and 'on to' sets that after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest who has signed the hotel register on arrival has been registered, formally checked in.

clue.text: Cowardly eccentric shows caution

parts.note: yellow is slang for cowardly
a card is an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: A timid oddball displays some carefulness.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a referee's booking, shown with a yellow card, is formally called a caution.

clue.text: Psychologist given November in prison

indicators.note: November is placed in the prison, so one is put inside the other

parts.note: jug is slang for prison
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A psychologist is jailed in the month of November.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Jung was the Swiss founder of analytical psychology, so a famous psychologist.

clue.text: Cannot impose change in financial restitution

indicators.note: the letters of cannot impose are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: An authority is unable to force a change in how money is repaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Compensation is money paid to make good a loss, which is restitution.

clue.text: Dog with others that pretend to fight

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the people who do so, matching the plural noun

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely, to shadow them
boxers are another breed of dog, so other dogs alongside the first

explanation.surface: A dog and its companions put on a mock fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' reads as the animal but is the verb meaning follow; 'others' leans on the dog theme, boxers being a breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadow boxing is sparring against an imaginary opponent, so those doing it go through the motions of combat without a real opponent.

clue.text: From lover, a heartless lie leads to trouble

indicators.note: the trimmed lie comes before trouble, leading to it
the lie loses its central letter, its heart

parts.note: a fiction is a lie
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A lover's cold-hearted untruth ends in strife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes T, the middle letter of FICTION, leaving FICION.
explanation.definitionFit: An aficionado is an enthusiast, someone who loves a particular activity.

clue.text: How one lost by getting up late?

definitions.text: How one lost by getting up late?

parts.words: How one lost by getting up late?
parts.note: reads like oversleeping, but a boxer who gets up off the canvas too late after a knockdown loses this way

explanation.surface: Someone missed out by oversleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer is counted out when they fail to rise before the referee counts to ten, so they lose the bout.

clue.text: Cabaret puzzles completely: in what way?

parts.note: to floor someone is to baffle them totally
how means in what way

explanation.surface: A nightclub act is utterly baffling: how is it done?
explanation.definitionFit: A floor show is a sequence of entertainment acts at a nightclub, which is what a cabaret is.

clue.text: Are behind working islander

indicators.note: the letters of are behind are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone from an island is behind with their work.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebridean is a native of the Hebrides, the islands off western Scotland.

clue.text: Hope everyone can contain bug

indicators.note: the words Hope everyone hold the answer within them, as a can holds its contents

explanation.surface: Optimism that the whole group can keep an infection in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can contain' looks like a statement about stopping a bug spreading; it signals the answer sitting inside 'Hope everyone'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet peeve is an irritation, and to bug someone is to annoy them; as a noun, bug likewise means an annoyance.

clue.text: Barge in here perhaps with tin (aluminium)

parts.note: a can is a tin container
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A boat's metal construction, tin and aluminium, invites a crafty description.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barge in' looks like interrupting rudely; it is the boat, and the 'perhaps' marks a barge as one example of what floats here.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is a man-made waterway where barges commonly travel, so a barge might be found in one.

clue.text: All numbers from 2 up are impossible to understand

definitions.meaning: every whole number greater than 1 lies past one on the number line
too hard for one to grasp

explanation.surface: Numbers from two upwards are baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the numbers past 1; idiomatically, what is beyond one's understanding.

clue.text: Civil reactor in more than dangerous state?

definitions.text: Civil reactor in more than dangerous state?

indicators.note: a reactor in a dangerous state is out of order, so the letters of civil reactor are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nuclear power station's reactor is beyond the danger point.
explanation.walkthrough: A reactor is critical once it sustains a chain reaction, so one beyond that is over critical; read as one word it means excessively fault-finding.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcritical means excessively critical; a reactor beyond critical would be literally overcritical.

clue.text: I had left leading lady with little to do

definitions.note: read as comparative, having less to do

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the nation's leading lady

explanation.surface: An actress walked out of a leading role that gave her little to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading lady' suggests a star actress; it is the Queen, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Idler is the comparative of idle, unoccupied, so more lacking in tasks.

clue.text: Secure-sounding Asian

indicators.note: the word for secure is heard, not spelt, so a different word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: to tie something is to secure it

explanation.surface: An Asian person who sounds safe and steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thai is a person from Thailand, a South-East Asian country.

clue.text: Hypocrite pitches right into greedy guts

indicators.note: the letter for right is thrown in, as if pitched
the letter goes inside the greedy guts

parts.note: a pig is a greedy person, a greedy guts

explanation.surface: A two-faced person launches a just attack on a glutton.
explanation.definitionFit: A prig is a self-righteous person who affects superior virtue, close to a hypocrite.

clue.text: A cat is a tiny little thing

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A kitten is described as a tiny little creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest unit of an element, and figuratively a minute quantity.

clue.text: Supporter chucking coin in the water?

definitions.meaning: someone who wishes another well, a backer
read literally, one who makes a wish at a wishing well by tossing in a coin

explanation.surface: A fan throws money into a fountain or pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-wisher is someone who hopes for another's success; the joke reads it as a person wishing at a well.

clue.text: River craft have no British cereal

indicators.note: the river craft lack the letter for British, so it is taken away

parts.note: boats are river craft

explanation.surface: Riverboats carry no British grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cereal crop grown for its grain, as in porridge.

clue.text: Coming in ungrammatically is delightful

definitions.meaning: treating the noun entrance as a verb and adding -ing gives a clumsy form for making an entrance

explanation.surface: An awkwardly worded arrival is charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrancing means enchanting; jokingly it is also the made-up verb form of entrance, arriving.
